title: Carnival pay and saving money on the Royal American
summary: He explains how costs shrank carnival wages, the Royal American bonus, and how he saved money gambling.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Now how'd you make out with carnivals? Did they pay well? Those little shows?
Yeah, but take up all your money to live on them carnivals.
How much would they pay a week?

Well they say seventy dollars a week. You got a birth, you sleep in a birth, they're going to take out for that. You got to eat with them, they're going to charge you like the devil on that train eating, see. And you got to pay big money for your food, your cigarettes, your smoke, see. And when you finish up you're making about forty dollars a week, I don't want to call it, when you finish paying out of everything, you know what I mean?
That's the same for Mac, Billy Mac, and the same for Solid Screen and American, whatever you want.

All that's the same, you make good salary but the money would go, you have to let it go for your living expenses, you got laundry and all that stuff, they don't pay for nothing for you, you got to pay for everything. Mm-hmm. For yourself.

Well one thing I like about the Royal American, every time you go out with them, they pay the same money, but when you start, the day you start to wake, you're boneless start. And when you get back and go in, you got a hundred and fifty dollar bonus. Your salary would be like four to five dollars a week, after taking expenses out. Well if you can save any of that back and you get back and put that hundred and fifty with it where you got you something. I know fellas come back and have six hundred dollars, six hundred dollars, something like that. The best I ever did was five, I come back with five, one year.
That was for one summer, you came back with five hundred dollars?
Well you did all right, I never did that well.

Yeah I did all right that summer. And Solid Screen show, how I got lucky there, they would gamble every pity. Played what you call strip poker, they played it hard too, but heavy. And I'd lose my pity, heavy pity I'd lose. So a couple of weeks there, something got ill, me and I got lucky, and I wanted me about seven dollars, about three hundred dollars this week, about three hundred dollars next week. So I just banked all that in the bottom of my trunk, I wouldn't touch it, I'd leave it on my side until we come in. I come in that year, about four hundred and something dollars. That's by me saving it, you know.
